title: A stream meets a dam
hook: A structure in a stream can change a nearby habitat.

knows: Animals depend on features of their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: A beaver builds a dam across a stream. What can happen to water immediately upstream?

misconception: A single observation or change determines the same outcome everywhere.
objective: A beaver builds a dam across a stream. What can happen to water immediately upstream?

claims.text: A beaver builds a dam across a stream. What can happen to water immediately upstream? The first panel shows a flowing channel; the second shows a dam with water collecting upstream. Beaver dams can slow and impound water, creating pond or wetland habitat. Actual extent and effects depend on the stream, terrain and dam.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: US Geological Survey, beaver and wetlands, https://www.usgs.gov/

claims.text: The panels show a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
Water collects on the uphill side of an obstruction in a stream. Which side is upstream? Upstream is the direction from which the flow approaches.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: US Geological Survey, beaver and wetlands, https://www.usgs.gov/

recall.question: Water collects on the uphill side of an obstruction in a stream. Which side is upstream?
options: The side where the water approaches the obstruction
The side where water has already passed
recall.why: Upstream is the direction from which the flow approaches.
